articles.title: Hackers Used Meta’s AI Support Bot to Seize Instagram Accounts
articles.summary: Microsoft just dropped fixes for nearly 200 security holes in one Patch Tuesday—apparently they've been saving them up like Pokémon cards. Three dozen earned the coveted 'critical' rating, because why patch incrementally when you can have one glorious dumpster fire?

articles.title: Microsoft's worst 'Nightmare' unleashes BitLocker bypass 0-day
articles.summary: ShinyHunters claims they pwned 100 organizations using an Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day, starting with University of Nottingham. When your enterprise software has more holes than Swiss cheese, maybe it's time to reconsider that vendor relationship.

articles.title: VRChat says somebody faked a breach notice with the Maine AG's office
articles.summary: Microsoft's BitLocker gets yet another bypass courtesy of researcher 'Nightmare'—because apparently Microsoft's idea of encryption is more like a polite suggestion. Another day, another Windows exploit dropping like it's hot.

articles.title: The Gentlemen Ransomware Claims 478 Victims, Can Spread Like a Worm
articles.summary: GreatXML exploit bypasses BitLocker via recovery partition XML files, discovered accidentally in just 4 hours. When your 'secure' disk encryption can be defeated by parsing some XML, maybe it's time to admit defeat and go back to hiding files in fake calculator apps.

articles.title: Netherlands Seizes 800 Servers, Arrests 2 for Aiding Cyberattacks
articles.summary: Hackers seized Obama's Instagram and Space Force accounts by tricking Meta's AI support bot into resetting passwords. Nothing says 'cutting-edge security' like getting owned by social engineering a chatbot that's dumber than a box of rocks.

articles.title: Yes to California's Bill to Ban Surveillance Pricing
articles.summary: CISA contractor 'accidentally' published AWS GovCloud keys and agency secrets on public GitHub, now Congress wants answers. When the cybersecurity agency can't secure its own secrets, it's like hiring a pyromaniac as fire chief.

articles.title: France’s ‘sovereign’ messenger Tchap was breached, and officials and the hacker disagree on how badly
articles.summary: France's 'sovereign' government messaging platform Tchap got breached through account hijacking. Building your own secure messenger to avoid trusting WhatsApp, only to get pwned anyway—that's some premium government-grade irony right there.

articles.title: Phishing Attack Volume Down 20%, but Risk Still Rising
articles.summary: EFF drops the ultimatum on Section 702: warrant requirement or bust as Congress keeps kicking the surveillance can down the road. The mass surveillance authority's expiration deadline looms while lawmakers play hot potato with our civil liberties.

articles.title: A Point-by-Point Breakdown of Trump’s Failed Iran War Objectives
articles.summary: Hakeem Jeffries finally grew a spine as Democratic leaders rallied against extending the domestic spy law. Advocates are cautiously optimistic that centrist Democrats switched sides, but warn against any extension of this constitutional dumpster fire.

articles.title: ‘News’ Site Keeps Hallucinating EFF Staffers
articles.summary: EFF backs California's bill to ban surveillance pricing—the corporate practice of charging different prices based on harvested personal data. Because nothing says 'free market' like algorithmically screwing customers based on their browsing history.
